title: KINETIC
subtitle: Labor and interruption — coordinated work rhythms broken by maintenance and rest
lineage: Primary: SCION 083 (Berlin: Symphony of a Great City) · Supporting: SCION 079 (Qatsi), SCION 078 (Samsara)
theorem: Make a passage from three documented work processes. Establish a repeated movement in each, briefly coordinate their rhythms through a sound phrase, break that coordination with one complete maintenance/waiting interval at normal speed, widen to context, and end when a mechanism stops.
boundary_note: Contextual wide shots prevent the shared rhythmic pulse from erasing the different historical conditions of watchmaking (1947), weaving, and auto assembly (1936).

v1_defect_timecodes: Optional v2 enhancement — Seg #05 (t=18.60s-23.80s): Upgrade 'THREE WORKSHOPS ALIGNED' from a single-stream shot to a synchronized 3-panel triptych locking Processes 01, 02, and 03 visually to the pulse.
critic_tribunal.largest_gap: All v1 shots were clean and cut-free; upgrading Seg #05 to a 3-panel triptych makes the three-workshop rhythmic coordination visually explicit.
critic_tribunal.causal_hypothesis: Single-stream segment mode used in v1 for Seg #05.
critic_tribunal.falsifiable_repair: Use `mode='triptych'` with `clips=['6ee8ef44', '9b8b1f1e', 'aeebdc87']` in Seg #05 so watchmaking, loom shuttle, and factory stamping lock together visually before the normal-speed maintenance interruption (`2ab95576`).
critic_tribunal.strength_to_preserve: All three work processes, the normal-speed bearing-oiling maintenance interruption (`2ab95576`), the wide factory-floor contextual reveal (`eba7d1c4`), and the worker stopping at the close (`135e3a64`).
